chapter: Musicians of the era: players, drummers, bassists, pianists
title: Erroll Garner in Pittsburgh and Art Tatum's help
summary: Jackson and Danny Barker took teenage Erroll Garner around Pittsburgh houses and urged him to come to New York, where Tatum looked after him.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: What about the little kid, the little short kid from Pittsburgh, Erroll Garner?

Oh, well, let's don't even mention him. Do you know, when we used to play Pittsburgh's Stanley Theater, Danny and I used to get him and take him out with us. He wasn't but about 17 years old and we used to take him -- Of course, you know, back in those days, you went to every place you wanted to go. You know, there was a lot of

-- in Pittsburgh. And we used to go around there, not to be a purchaser, but we used to like to go hang around -- Danny used to like to go talk to the girls. And we used to take Erroll Garner around there to play for them. If his father knew that --

-- you know? And Danny told him -- Danny Barker used to tell him, he said, "You better come to New York because there's nobody in New York played like you, nobody." He said, "Why don't you get yourself together and come on to the big city so you can be somewhere and get someplace?" Danny Barker talked to him then about that.

So we come to New York and, I don't know, I think we was playing at the Park Central Hotel and we looked up and we went down 52nd Street and down to Tondelayo's and here's Erroll Garner sitting up there playing.

That's right. And, of course, Art was in the street then, you know, and Art did him just like Fats did Art. Art Tatum took Erroll Garner in his hand. Erroll was scared to death. The guys used to laugh at him, and
Art told him, he said, "Don't pay them no attention. You go ahead and play your piano, boy, like you want to play it."
Yeah. But Art labeled him, though. Art labeled him. Art told him that he was a piano player like a piano player that plays in a house of ill repute, you know. I can't use the word, you know, --
Yeah, well, we know the word.
And Erroll never read a note of music and his brother studied -- his brother was a good pianist -- his brother studied like everything. His brother never could play like Erroll could.
Butter, do you remember what his name was?
He was Timmy Rogers' accompanist for a long time -- the comedian, Timmy Rogers? --
-- he was his accompanist for a long time, Linton was. And can arrange. Linton can arrange. He's a nice arranger.
But Erroll didn't study. He didn't read a note.
Lightning only struck once in his family.
And then Hank Jones' family it struck three or four times.
